issue.title: Can't use masked and union together
Describe incorrectly handles 'true' and 'false' types
issue.body:
Hey, Ian!

I found a problem while trying to write a struct for a described exact boolean value:
```typescript
const _true: Describe<true> = literal(true);
```

That's what we got here:
```
Type 'Struct<false, false>' is not assignable to type 'Describe<false>'.
  Types of property 'schema' are incompatible.
    Type 'false' is not assignable to type 'null'.ts(2322)
```

On the other hand, this code is correct:
```typescript
const _42: Describe<42> = literal(42);
```

Describe is using utility type `StructSchema`, so it seems that this type has a bug:
```typescript
let _42Schema: StructSchema<42>;           // 42
let _trueSchema: StructSchema<true>;       // null, but should be true
```

Here is the sandbox: https://codesandbox.io/s/fast-water-t00d7

issue.title: Refinement for top level object failed when field has refinement
Rename files to `cjs.js` for compatibility with React Native
issue.body:
Importing @solana/web3.js in React Native throws the following error.

```
error: Error: While trying to resolve module `superstruct` from file `/Users/sluscher/mobile-wallet-adapter/js/node_modules/@solana/web3.js/lib/index.browser.cjs.js`, the package `/Users/sluscher/mobile-wallet-adapter/js/node_modules/superstruct/package.json` was successfully found. However, this package itself specifies a `main` module field that could not be resolved (`/Users/sluscher/mobile-wallet-adapter/js/node_modules/superstruct/lib/index.cjs`. Indeed, none of these files exist:

  * /Users/sluscher/mobile-wallet-adapter/js/node_modules/superstruct/lib/index.cjs(.native|.android.js|.native.js|.js|.android.json|.native.json|.json|.android.ts|.native.ts|.ts|.android.tsx|.native.tsx|.tsx)
```

You can see that the React Native packager expects a `.js` extension in addition to `.cjs`

If `superstruct` could rename the CommonJS bundles from `.cjs` to `.cjs.js` that would make it Just Work™ for React Native folks!

More details on the problem here, if you're interested: https://github.com/facebook/metro/issues/535

issue.title: No longer possible to coerce values to `undefined`
issue.body:
If I return `undefined` from a coercion, the coercion is ignored completely, and the original value is kept (even if the original value does not satisfy the struct we're coercing the value into).

The most common use case in my project is:

```ts
const coercableOptional = <T>(struct: Struct<T>) =>
  coerce(optional(struct), literal(null), () => undefined);
```

This no longer works: `null` values are retained, even if `struct` should not allow null values.

I think this was caused by #1106

Is there an alternative syntax for coercing to undefined, or is this a bug that needs fixing?
